premises.text: Existing competitive programming sites focus on textbook algorithms, not real-world engineering problems
premises.evidence_span: sites like ACM and Topcoder focus on a small set of textbook algorithms, whereas in the real world, you work on things ranging from machine learning to artificial intelligence to distributed systems

premises.text: HackerRank is a competitive platform for hackers to solve real-world problems
premises.evidence_span: we are building the competitive lead for hackers to solve real world problems

premises.text: Challenges span types and ten dynamically ranked difficulty levels based on how many users solve them
premises.evidence_span: we're going to have a variety of challenges classified into 10 levels of difficulty. The difficulty level of a challenge is determined by the number of users who solve it

premises.text: Companies contribute real datasets and problems they are actually working on
premises.evidence_span: we are inviting companies to give us real data sets or problems that they're actually working on

premises.text: In-browser coding across languages with compile/test, bot-vs-bot play, and visualization
premises.evidence_span: you can compile and code right inside our interface

premises.text: Archived challenges release code snippets so hackers can learn optimal algorithms from others
premises.evidence_span: archive the challenges every two weeks, and release all the code snippets so that hackers can learn from others to write optimal algorithms

premises.text: Centralizes the world's most interesting problems that currently run as scattered hackathons and contests
premises.evidence_span: We are building the largest collection of the world's most interesting problems for hackers to solve

value.text: Hackers compete on and learn from real-world programming problems online

causal_links.evidence_span: how much fun it would be to have a competitive site for real world problems
building the competitive lead for hackers to solve real world problems

notes: Signup/game-count and time-on-site metrics excluded as traction. Stripe/Netflix contest sizes used only as context for centralization premise (P7).
